source.text: Ἀδελφοί μου, μὴ ἐν προσωπολημψίαις ἔχετε τὴν πίστιν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τῆς δόξης;

records.literal_gloss: Brothers of me, not with partialities hold you the faith of the Lord of us Jesus Christ of the glory?

en.L: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, you do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} of glory with acts of favoritism, [do you]?
en.B: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, you do not hold the faith of our glorious Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} while you show favoritism, do you?
en.R: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, you have faith in our glorious Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. So how can you treat some people as more important than others?

es.L: Hermanos míos, no {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} la fe de nuestro Señor Jesús {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} de la gloria con favoritismos, ¿[verdad]?
es.B: Hermanos míos, no {{plural_you:mantienen|mantenéis}} la fe de nuestro glorioso Señor Jesús {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} mientras {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} distinción entre las personas, ¿verdad?
es.R: Hermanos míos, {{plural_you:ustedes tienen|vosotros tenéis}} fe en nuestro glorioso Señor Jesús {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}. Entonces, ¿cómo {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} tratar a unas personas como si valieran más que otras?

fr.L: Mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, ce n’est pas avec des marques de partialité que vous tenez la foi de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} de gloire, [n’est-ce pas] ?
fr.B: Mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, vous ne tenez pas la foi en notre glorieux Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} tout en faisant du favoritisme, n’est-ce pas ?
fr.R: Mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, vous avez foi en notre glorieux Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. Alors, comment pouvez-vous traiter certaines personnes comme plus importantes que d’autres ?

sw.L: Ndugu zangu, hamuishiki imani ya Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} wa utukufu pamoja na matendo ya upendeleo, [sivyo]?
sw.B: Ndugu zangu, hamwezi kuishika imani ya Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} mwenye utukufu huku mkiwapendelea watu, sivyo?
sw.R: Ndugu zangu, mna imani katika Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} mwenye utukufu. Basi mnawezaje kuwatendea watu wengine kana kwamba ni bora kuliko wengine?

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no, as the SBLGNT punctuates it
alternatives: a command: "do not hold the faith ... with favoritism"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT ends the sentence with a question mark, and μὴ with a question expects the answer "no": surely you do not combine the two. Read without the question mark, ἔχετε is a command, "do not hold". Either way James says that faith in Christ and favoritism cannot go together; only the form differs.

decisions.choice: acts of favoritism: treating people differently by how they look or what they own
decisions.reason: προσωπολημψία is built from the Hebrew idiom "to lift the face" of someone, that is, to show them favor. The law forbids it in court, whether the favor goes to the poor or to the powerful (Leviticus 19:15; Deuteronomy 1:17). The plural means repeated acts of it, and verses 2-4 give an example.

decisions.choice: the faith of our Lord: faith in our Lord Jesus Christ
alternatives: the faithfulness that Jesus himself showed
decisions.reason: The genitive could name the one believed in or the one whose faith it is. James speaks of faith as something believers have and must show (2:14, 18), so here it is faith that rests on Jesus as Lord.

decisions.choice: of glory: describes the Lord, "our glorious Lord"
alternatives: "Jesus Christ, who is the Glory" (the presence of God among his people)
decisions.reason: δόξης stands at the end of the phrase with its own article and can be read several ways. Taking it with "Lord" gives "our glorious Lord". Some read it as a title, "the Glory", recalling the glory of God that filled the tabernacle (Exodus 40:34). The contrast is the same on any reading: people honor gold rings and fine clothes (2:2) while their Lord is the glorious one.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: James is writing to the whole community of believers, women and men alike, so the inclusive form is the default; the traditional wording is the alternative.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal follows the Greek, which has no article here.

decisions.choice: you have faith ... So how can you ...?
alternatives: you do not hold ... do you?
decisions.reason: Readable makes two short sentences: a statement of their faith, then a question that expects the same answer as the Greek, that the two do not belong together.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As in Romans and Philippians, Spanish "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, so it carries no gender setting in James.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: James writes to his readers in the plural throughout. Each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (default) or vosotros. Where he turns to one imagined hearer (2:11, 2:18-22) Spanish uses "tú" with no setting.

decisions.choice: des marques de partialité (L); faire du favoritisme (B); also 2:9
decisions.reason: "Faire acception de personnes" is the traditional church phrase but is no longer understood. "Partialité" keeps the noun at Literal; "favoritisme" is the everyday word for treating people by their rank or wealth (m2), as the English "favoritism".

decisions.choice: ndugu, no setting
alternatives: ndugu wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already includes sisters, and "mtu" (2:14, 2:20) includes women, so the Swahili of this chapter has no gender spans.

source.text: ἐὰν γὰρ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς συναγωγὴν ὑμῶν ἀνὴρ χρυσοδακτύλιος ἐν ἐσθῆτι λαμπρᾷ, εἰσέλθῃ δὲ καὶ πτωχὸς ἐν ῥυπαρᾷ ἐσθῆτι, ἐπιβλέψητε δὲ ἐπὶ τὸν φοροῦντα τὴν ἐσθῆτα τὴν λαμπρὰν καὶ εἴπητε· Σὺ κάθου ὧδε καλῶς, καὶ τῷ πτωχῷ εἴπητε· Σὺ στῆθι ἢ κάθου ἐκεῖ ὑπὸ τὸ ὑποπόδιόν μου, οὐ διεκρίθητε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς καὶ ἐγένεσθε κριταὶ διαλογισμῶν πονηρῶν;

records.literal_gloss: If for comes into assembly of you a man gold-ringed in clothing bright, comes in and also a poor [man] in filthy clothing, \v 3 look you and upon the [one] wearing the clothing the bright and say, You sit here well, and to the poor [man] say, You stand or sit there under the footstool of me, \v 4 not made distinctions you among yourselves and became judges of thoughts evil?

en.L: For if a man with gold rings, in bright clothing, comes into your assembly, and a poor [man] in filthy clothing also comes in, \v 3 and you look with favor on the one wearing the bright clothing and say, "You sit here in a good [place]," and to the poor [man] you say, "You stand," or, "Sit there under my footstool," \v 4 have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
en.B: Say a man comes into your assembly with gold rings on his fingers and dressed in splendid clothes, and a poor man comes in too, in dirty clothes. \v 3 You give your attention to the man in the splendid clothes and tell him, "Take this good seat here," and you tell the poor man, "Stand," or, "Sit on the floor down by my footstool." \v 4 Have you not drawn distinctions among yourselves and become judges whose reasoning is evil?
en.R: Imagine that a man comes into your meeting wearing gold rings and fine clothes. Then a poor man comes in too, wearing dirty clothes. \v 3 You pay special attention to the man in fine clothes and say to him, "Please sit here in this good seat." But you say to the poor man, "Stand," or, "Sit on the floor by my feet." \v 4 If you do this, are you not treating people unequally? Are you not judging them with evil thoughts?

es.L: Porque si en {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} asamblea entra un hombre con anillos de oro, con ropa espléndida, y entra también un pobre con ropa mugrienta, \v 3 y {{plural_you:miran|miráis}} con favor al que lleva la ropa espléndida y le {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «Tú siéntate aquí, en un buen [lugar]», y al pobre le {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «Tú quédate de pie», o: «Siéntate allí, bajo mi escabel», \v 4 ¿no {{plural_you:han hecho|habéis hecho}} distinciones entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos y {{plural_you:han llegado|habéis llegado}} a ser jueces con malos pensamientos?
es.B: Supongamos que en {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} asamblea entra un hombre con anillos de oro en los dedos y vestido con ropa espléndida, y que entra también un pobre con ropa sucia. \v 3 {{plural_you:Ustedes atienden|Vosotros atendéis}} al de la ropa espléndida y le {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «Toma este buen asiento», y al pobre le {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «Quédate de pie», o: «Siéntate en el suelo, junto a mi escabel». \v 4 ¿No {{plural_you:han hecho|habéis hecho}} distinciones entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y {{plural_you:se han convertido|os habéis convertido}} en jueces que razonan con maldad?
es.R: {{plural_you:Imaginen|Imaginad}} que un hombre entra en {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} reunión con anillos de oro y ropa fina. Luego entra también un pobre con ropa sucia. \v 3 {{plural_you:Ustedes atienden|Vosotros atendéis}} de forma especial al hombre de la ropa fina y le {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «Por favor, siéntate aquí, en este buen asiento». Pero al pobre le {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «Quédate de pie», o: «Siéntate en el suelo, a mis pies». \v 4 Si {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} esto, ¿no {{plural_you:están|estáis}} tratando a las personas de manera desigual? ¿No {{plural_you:están|estáis}} juzgándolas con malos pensamientos?

fr.L: Car s’il entre dans votre assemblée un homme aux bagues d’or, en vêtement éclatant, et qu’entre aussi un pauvre en vêtement sale, \v 3 et que vous portiez vos regards sur celui qui porte le vêtement éclatant et disiez : « Toi, assieds-toi ici, à la bonne [place] », et que vous disiez au pauvre : « Toi, tiens-toi debout », ou : « Assieds-toi là, sous mon marchepied », \v 4 n’avez-vous pas fait des distinctions entre vous, et n’êtes-vous pas devenus des juges aux pensées mauvaises ?
fr.B: Supposons qu’un homme entre dans votre assemblée avec des bagues d’or aux doigts et des vêtements magnifiques, et qu’entre aussi un pauvre aux vêtements sales. \v 3 Vous accordez toute votre attention à l’homme aux vêtements magnifiques et vous lui dites : « Prends cette bonne place, ici », et vous dites au pauvre : « Toi, reste debout », ou : « Assieds-toi par terre, près de mon marchepied. » \v 4 N’avez-vous pas fait des distinctions entre vous, et n’êtes-vous pas devenus des juges aux raisonnements mauvais ?
fr.R: Imaginez qu’un homme entre dans votre réunion. Il porte des bagues en or et de beaux vêtements. Ensuite un pauvre entre aussi, avec des vêtements sales. \v 3 Vous faites très attention à l’homme aux beaux vêtements et vous lui dites : « Viens t’asseoir ici, à cette bonne place. » Mais au pauvre, vous dites : « Toi, reste debout », ou : « Assieds-toi par terre, à mes pieds. » \v 4 Si vous agissez ainsi, ne traitez-vous pas les gens de manière inégale ? Ne les jugez-vous pas avec de mauvaises pensées ?

sw.L: Kwa maana akiingia katika kusanyiko lenu mtu mwenye pete za dhahabu, katika mavazi ya kung'aa, na akiingia pia maskini katika mavazi machafu, \v 3 nanyi mkimtazama kwa upendeleo yule aliyevaa mavazi ya kung'aa na kumwambia, "Wewe keti hapa mahali pazuri," na kumwambia yule maskini, "Wewe simama," au, "Keti pale chini ya kibao changu cha kuwekea miguu," \v 4 je, hamkufanya ubaguzi kati yenu wenyewe, na kuwa waamuzi wenye mawazo maovu?
sw.B: Tuseme mtu anaingia katika kusanyiko lenu akiwa na pete za dhahabu vidoleni na mavazi ya fahari, kisha anaingia pia maskini mwenye nguo chafu. \v 3 Mnamjali yule aliyevaa mavazi ya fahari na kumwambia, "Keti hapa mahali hapa pazuri," na yule maskini mnamwambia, "Simama," au, "Keti sakafuni karibu na kibao changu cha kuwekea miguu." \v 4 Je, hamjafanya ubaguzi kati yenu wenyewe, mkawa waamuzi wanaofikiri kwa uovu?
sw.R: Fikirini kwamba mtu anaingia katika mkutano wenu amevaa pete za dhahabu na nguo nzuri sana. Kisha maskini anaingia pia, amevaa nguo chafu. \v 3 Mnamjali sana yule mwenye nguo nzuri na kumwambia, "Karibu, keti hapa kwenye kiti hiki kizuri." Lakini maskini mnamwambia, "Simama," au, "Keti chini sakafuni karibu na miguu yangu." \v 4 Mkifanya hivyo, je, hamwatendei watu bila usawa? Je, hamwahukumu kwa mawazo maovu?

decisions.choice: your assembly: the gathering of believers, or the place where it meets
alternatives: a church meeting held to settle a dispute between members
decisions.reason: συναγωγή is the word for a Jewish synagogue, a gathering or its building. James uses it for the Christian meeting, as a letter to Jewish believers naturally would (1:1); in 5:14 he speaks of the church. The talk of judges (2:4) and courts (2:6) has suggested to some that this is a meeting to hear a case, but the scene reads just as well as an ordinary gathering for worship.

decisions.choice: gold rings and bright clothes: signs of wealth and rank
decisions.reason: χρυσοδακτύλιος means "gold-fingered": wearing gold rings, perhaps several. In the Roman world a gold ring marked a man of high rank, and bright, clean clothing showed wealth (Luke 23:11 uses the same adjective of the robe Herod put on Jesus). The poor man's clothes are ῥυπαρᾷ, "filthy": he has no change of clothing.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "stand, or sit there under my footstool"
alternatives: "stand there, or sit here under my footstool"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ in where "there" and "here" fall in the second speech. The SBLGNT puts "there" with "sit". Many later manuscripts read "stand there, or sit here under my footstool". The insult is the same either way: the poor man is left standing or put on the floor. From general knowledge; reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: made distinctions among yourselves: treated people as of different worth
alternatives: "been divided in yourselves", wavering in your faith, as διακρίνω means in 1:6
decisions.reason: διεκρίθητε can mean "make a distinction" or, in the middle and passive, "be divided, doubt", as in 1:6. Both fit: they sort people by their clothes, and that shows a mind divided between faith in the glorious Lord (2:1) and the world's values. The first is the plainer sense here, given the scene.

decisions.choice: judges with evil thoughts: judges whose reasoning is wrong
decisions.reason: The genitive διαλογισμῶν πονηρῶν describes the kind of judges they have become: they decide who deserves honor, and their reasoning is evil. Judging others belongs to God (4:11-12).

decisions.choice: on the floor down by my footstool; on the floor by my feet
decisions.reason: "Under my footstool" means sitting on the floor at the speaker's feet, the place of least honor. Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: two questions
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long question in two and adds "If you do this" to tie it back to the scene.

decisions.choice: tú in the quoted words to the rich man and the poor man
alternatives: usted to the rich man, tú to the poor man
decisions.reason: The Greek says Σὺ to both men. Giving the rich man "usted" and the poor man "tú" would dramatise the favoritism vividly in Spanish, but it adds a contrast the Greek does not mark, so both are addressed with "tú", outside the plural_you setting.

decisions.choice: votre assemblée (L, B); votre réunion (R)
decisions.reason: The word here is the gathering of believers or its meeting place (m1), as the English "assembly" says. French "synagogue" would make readers think of a Jewish place of worship outside the church.

decisions.choice: "tu" to the rich man and to the poor man alike
alternatives: "vous" to the rich man, "tu" to the poor man
decisions.reason: The Greek uses the same singular to both. A polite "vous" for the rich man would add a contrast the text does not make; the difference lies in the seats offered.

source.text: ἀκούσατε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί.

records.literal_gloss: Listen, brothers of me beloved.

en.L: Listen, my beloved {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.B: Listen, my dear {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.R: Listen, my dear {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.

es.L: {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, hermanos míos amados.
es.B: {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, mis queridos hermanos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, mis queridos hermanos.

fr.L: Écoutez, mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} bien-aimés.
fr.B: Écoutez, mes chers {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}.
fr.R: Écoutez, mes chers {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}.

sw.L: Sikilizeni, ndugu zangu wapendwa.
sw.B: Sikilizeni, ndugu zangu wapendwa.
sw.R: Nisikilizeni, ndugu zangu wapendwa.

decisions.choice: listen: pay attention and take this in
decisions.reason: ἀκούσατε calls the readers to attend closely before the question that follows, as the prophets call Israel to hear (Deuteronomy 6:4). James wants them to hear and do (1:22).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: James is writing to the whole community of believers, women and men alike, so the inclusive form is the default; the traditional wording is the alternative. ἀγαπητός is rendered "beloved" at Literal and "dear" at Balanced and Readable, the warm everyday word.

source.text: οὐχ ὁ θεὸς ἐξελέξατο τοὺς πτωχοὺς τῷ κόσμῳ πλουσίους ἐν πίστει καὶ κληρονόμους τῆς βασιλείας ἧς ἐπηγγείλατο τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν;

records.literal_gloss: Not the God chose the poor to the world rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom which he promised to the [ones] loving him?

en.L: Did not God choose the poor in the world [to be] rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised to those who love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?
en.B: Has not God chosen those who are poor in the world's eyes to be rich in faith and to inherit the kingdom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised to those who love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?
en.R: God has chosen people who are poor in the world's eyes to be rich in faith, has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not? They will receive the kingdom that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised to those who love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: ¿No eligió Dios a los pobres según el mundo [para ser] ricos en fe y herederos del reino que prometió a los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} aman?
es.B: ¿No ha elegido Dios a los que son pobres a los ojos del mundo para que sean ricos en fe y hereden el reino que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} prometió a los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} aman?
es.R: Dios ha elegido a los que el mundo considera pobres para que sean ricos en fe, ¿no es así? Ellos recibirán el reino que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} prometió a los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} aman.

fr.L: Dieu n’a-t-il pas choisi les pauvres quant au monde [pour être] riches en foi et héritiers du royaume qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a promis à ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}aiment ?
fr.B: Dieu n’a-t-il pas choisi ceux que le monde tient pour pauvres afin qu’ils soient riches dans la foi et qu’ils reçoivent en héritage le royaume qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a promis à ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}aiment ?
fr.R: Dieu a choisi des gens qui sont pauvres aux yeux du monde pour qu’ils soient riches dans la foi, n’est-ce pas ? Ils recevront le royaume qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a promis à ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}aiment.

sw.L: Je, Mungu hakuwachagua maskini kwa ulimwengu [wawe] matajiri katika imani na warithi wa ufalme aliowaahidi wale wampendao?
sw.B: Je, Mungu hajawachagua wale walio maskini machoni pa ulimwengu ili wawe matajiri katika imani na kuurithi ufalme aliowaahidi wale wanaompenda?
sw.R: Mungu amewachagua watu ambao ulimwengu unawaona kuwa maskini ili wawe matajiri katika imani, sivyo? Wao watapokea ufalme aliowaahidi wale wanaompenda.

decisions.choice: the poor in the world: poor as the world counts wealth
decisions.reason: The dative κόσμῳ without a preposition means "poor with respect to the world", that is, in the world's reckoning. The two readings come to much the same thing: they have little of what the world values. The contrast follows at once: rich in faith.

decisions.choice: rich in faith: their wealth lies in the sphere of faith
alternatives: rich because they have a great deal of faith
decisions.reason: James is not saying that poor people have more faith. He says God has made them rich in what counts: by faith they belong to his kingdom. The verb chose has a double object, "chose the poor ... to be rich".

decisions.choice: heirs of the kingdom promised to those who love him
decisions.reason: Jesus said, "Blessed are you poor, because the kingdom of God is yours" (Luke 6:20; Matthew 5:3). "Promised to those who love him" repeats 1:12, where the crown of life is promised in the same words.

decisions.choice: to inherit; they will receive
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what being an heir means: the kingdom will be theirs.

decisions.choice: statement with a tag question
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a statement with "has he not?" so that the expected answer, yes, is plain.

source.text: ὑμεῖς δὲ ἠτιμάσατε τὸν πτωχόν.

records.literal_gloss: You but dishonored the poor.

en.L: But you dishonored the poor [man].
en.B: But you have dishonored the poor.
en.R: But you have treated poor people with contempt.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes deshonraron|vosotros deshonrasteis}} al pobre.
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes han deshonrado|vosotros habéis deshonrado}} al pobre.
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes han tratado|vosotros habéis tratado}} con desprecio a los pobres.

fr.L: Mais vous, vous avez déshonoré le pauvre.
fr.B: Mais vous, vous avez déshonoré les pauvres.
fr.R: Mais vous, vous avez traité les pauvres avec mépris.

sw.L: Lakini ninyi mlimvunjia heshima yule maskini.
sw.B: Lakini ninyi mmewavunjia heshima maskini.
sw.R: Lakini ninyi mmewadharau watu maskini.

decisions.choice: dishonored: treated with contempt, put to shame
decisions.reason: ἠτιμάσατε is the opposite of giving honor. In a culture where honor was publicly given and withheld, sending the poor man to the floor (2:3) shamed him in front of everyone, and so dishonored the people God has chosen (2:5).

decisions.choice: the poor: the poor man of verses 2-3, and the poor in general
alternatives: only the man in the example
decisions.reason: The article can point back to the man in the example or stand for the poor as a group, as in verse 5. The example stands for what they do to the poor.

decisions.choice: the poor; poor people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take the article as general, as the meaning decision says. Literal brackets "man" because the Greek adjective is masculine and verse 3 has a man in view.

decisions.choice: le pauvre (L), with no supplied word
decisions.reason: French uses the masculine adjective as a noun for the poor man of verses 2-3, so the English [man] is not needed.

source.text: οὐχ οἱ πλούσιοι καταδυναστεύουσιν ὑμῶν, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἕλκουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς κριτήρια;

records.literal_gloss: Not the rich oppress you, and they drag you into courts?

en.L: Is it not the rich who oppress you, and they themselves who drag you into courts?
en.B: Is it not the rich who exploit you? Are they not the very ones who drag you into court?
en.R: Are rich people not the ones who treat you harshly? Are they not the ones who drag you into court?

es.L: ¿No son los ricos los que {{plural_you:los|os}} oprimen, y ellos mismos los que {{plural_you:los|os}} arrastran a los tribunales?
es.B: ¿No son los ricos los que {{plural_you:los|os}} explotan? ¿No son ellos mismos los que {{plural_you:los|os}} llevan a rastras ante los jueces?
es.R: ¿No son los ricos los que {{plural_you:los|os}} tratan con dureza? ¿No son ellos los que {{plural_you:los|os}} arrastran a los tribunales?

fr.L: N’est-ce pas les riches qui vous oppriment, et eux-mêmes qui vous traînent devant les tribunaux ?
fr.B: N’est-ce pas les riches qui vous exploitent ? Ne sont-ils pas justement ceux qui vous traînent en justice ?
fr.R: Les riches ne sont-ils pas ceux qui vous traitent durement ? Ne sont-ils pas ceux qui vous traînent devant les juges ?

sw.L: Je, si matajiri wanaowadhulumu ninyi, na wao wenyewe wanaowaburuta mahakamani?
sw.B: Je, si matajiri ndio wanaowanyonya? Je, si wao hao wanaowaburuta mahakamani?
sw.R: Je, si matajiri ndio wanaowatendea kwa ukatili? Je, si wao wanaowapeleka mahakamani kwa nguvu?

decisions.choice: oppress: use power to exploit
decisions.reason: καταδυναστεύουσιν means to rule over someone harshly, to exploit by force. The prophets condemn the rich who crush the poor (Amos 4:1; 8:4). James will say the same in 5:4-6.

decisions.choice: drag you into courts: lawsuits by the powerful
decisions.reason: κριτήρια are law courts. A rich creditor or landowner could take a poor debtor to court and expect to win. The word "drag" suggests force and humiliation (Acts 16:19).

decisions.choice: the rich: the rich as a class, the ones they flatter
decisions.reason: The rich here are those outside the believers' community who use their power against them, as in 5:1-6. αὐτοὶ ("they themselves") stresses the irony: the very people the church flatters are the ones who mistreat it.

source.text: οὐκ αὐτοὶ βλασφημοῦσιν τὸ καλὸν ὄνομα τὸ ἐπικληθὲν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς;

records.literal_gloss: Not they blaspheme the good name the [one] having been called upon you?

en.L: Do they not blaspheme the good name that was called over you?
en.B: Are they not the ones who slander the honorable name that was spoken over you?
en.R: Are they not the ones who insult the good name of the Lord, the name that marks you as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people?

es.L: ¿No blasfeman ellos el buen nombre que fue invocado sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?
es.B: ¿No son ellos los que difaman el nombre honorable que fue pronunciado sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?
es.R: ¿No son ellos los que insultan el buen nombre del Señor, el nombre que {{plural_you:los|os}} señala como {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio pueblo?

fr.L: Ne sont-ce pas eux qui blasphèment le beau nom qui a été invoqué sur vous ?
fr.B: Ne sont-ce pas eux qui insultent le nom honorable qui a été prononcé sur vous ?
fr.R: Ne sont-ce pas eux qui insultent le beau nom du Seigneur, le nom qui montre que vous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} appartenez ?

sw.L: Je, si wao wanaolikufuru jina zuri lililotajwa juu yenu?
sw.B: Je, si wao ndio wanaolitukana jina lenye heshima lililotamkwa juu yenu?
sw.R: Je, si wao ndio wanaolitukana jina zuri la Bwana, jina linaloonyesha kwamba ninyi ni watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mwenyewe?

decisions.choice: the name called over you: the name that marks you as belonging to the Lord
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures, to have someone's name called over you means to belong to him (Deuteronomy 28:10; Amos 9:12, quoted in Acts 15:17). Believers were baptized in the name of Jesus (Acts 2:38), and so carry his name.

decisions.choice: blaspheme: speak against, revile
alternatives: slander only, without the sense of sin against God
decisions.reason: βλασφημοῦσιν means to speak evil of someone. Said of the Lord's name it is blasphemy. The rich may mock the name of Jesus, or slander his people; either way his name is dishonored.

decisions.choice: the good name: the name of the Lord Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: James has just spoken of "our glorious Lord Jesus Christ" (2:1), and believers bore his name. The name of God fits the Old Testament idiom too; the two are not far apart for James, who calls both God and Jesus "Lord".

decisions.choice: the good name of the Lord, the name that marks you as his own people
alternatives: the good name called over you
decisions.reason: Readable names whose name it is and explains the idiom.

decisions.choice: que vous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} appartenez (R)
decisions.reason: French says belonging with a verb and an object pronoun where the English has "his own people"; the span moves to that pronoun.

source.text: Εἰ μέντοι νόμον τελεῖτε βασιλικὸν κατὰ τὴν γραφήν Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν, καλῶς ποιεῖτε·

records.literal_gloss: If really law you fulfill royal according to the Scripture, You will love the neighbor of you as yourself, well you do;

en.L: If you really fulfill [the] royal law according to the Scripture, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you are doing well.
en.B: If you truly carry out the royal law as Scripture puts it, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you do well.
en.R: The King's great law is in Scripture: "Love your neighbor as you love yourself." If you really obey that law, you are doing what is right.

es.L: Si en verdad {{plural_you:cumplen|cumplís}} [la] ley real conforme a la Escritura: «Amarás a tu prójimo como a ti mismo», bien {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}.
es.B: Si de veras {{plural_you:cumplen|cumplís}} la ley real tal como la expresa la Escritura: «Amarás a tu prójimo como a ti mismo», {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} bien.
es.R: La gran ley del Rey está en la Escritura: «Ama a tu prójimo como te amas a ti mismo». Si de verdad {{plural_you:obedecen|obedecéis}} esa ley, {{plural_you:están|estáis}} haciendo lo correcto.

fr.L: Si toutefois vous accomplissez une loi royale, conformément à l’Écriture : « Tu aimeras ton prochain comme toi-même », vous agissez bien ;
fr.B: Si vous observez réellement la loi royale, telle que l’Écriture la formule : « Tu aimeras ton prochain comme toi-même », vous faites ce qui est bien.
fr.R: La grande loi du Roi se trouve dans l’Écriture : « Aime ton prochain comme tu t’aimes toi-même. » Si vous obéissez vraiment à cette loi, vous faites ce qui est juste.

sw.L: Ikiwa kweli mnaitimiza sheria ya kifalme kulingana na Maandiko, "Utampenda jirani yako kama wewe mwenyewe," mnafanya vema.
sw.B: Ikiwa kweli mnaitekeleza sheria ya kifalme kama Maandiko yanavyosema, "Utampenda jirani yako kama wewe mwenyewe," mnafanya vizuri.
sw.R: Sheria kuu ya Mfalme imo katika Maandiko: "Mpende jirani yako kama unavyojipenda mwenyewe." Mkiitii sheria hiyo kweli, mnatenda yaliyo sawa.

decisions.choice: really: if you truly keep the law, not just appear to
decisions.reason: μέντοι can strengthen ("really") or contrast ("however"). Here it sets the real keeping of the law against what they are doing to the poor: if they truly loved their neighbor, they would not shame him.

decisions.choice: the royal law: the law of the King, supreme over the rest
decisions.reason: βασιλικὸν means belonging to a king. This is the law of the kingdom just mentioned (2:5), given by its King, and it sums up all the commands (Matthew 22:39-40; Romans 13:9; Galatians 5:14).

decisions.choice: You shall love your neighbor as yourself: Leviticus 19:18
decisions.reason: James quotes Leviticus 19:18. A few verses earlier the same chapter forbids judges to favor either the poor or the great (Leviticus 19:15). So the law they claim to keep is the very law that condemns their favoritism.

decisions.choice: The King's great law
decisions.reason: Readable explains "royal": the law of the King, the most important one. It puts the quotation first so the condition is short.

decisions.choice: ley real
decisions.reason: "Ley real" is the settled term for James, but Spanish "real" also means "real, actual". The sentence's context ("conforme a la Escritura") points to the royal sense, and Readable spells it out as "la gran ley del Rey". A reviewer may prefer "ley regia" at Balanced to remove the ambiguity.

decisions.choice: une loi royale (L), la loi royale (B), la grande loi du Roi (R), lowercase; la Loi with a capital in 2:9-11 (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: Here "law" is the one command of love, called royal (m2), so it stays lowercase, as in "la loi de la liberté" (1:25, 2:12). From verse 9 on James speaks of the Law of Moses as a whole, which takes the capital, as the term sheet has it. Literal keeps the Greek's lack of an article.

decisions.choice: sheria ya kifalme
decisions.reason: "Sheria ya kifalme" (the royal law) is the settled term for James, an adjective like βασιλικὸν; Readable names the King, "sheria kuu ya Mfalme", as the English Readable does.

source.text: εἰ δὲ προσωπολημπτεῖτε, ἁμαρτίαν ἐργάζεσθε, ἐλεγχόμενοι ὑπὸ τοῦ νόμου ὡς παραβάται.

records.literal_gloss: If but you show partiality, sin you work, being convicted by the law as transgressors.

en.L: But if you show favoritism, you are committing sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.
en.B: But if you show favoritism, you commit sin, and the law convicts you as lawbreakers.
en.R: But if you favor some people over others, you are sinning. The law shows that you are guilty of breaking it.

es.L: Pero si {{plural_you:muestran|mostráis}} favoritismo, {{plural_you:cometen|cometéis}} pecado, y la ley {{plural_you:los|os}} declara culpables como transgresores.
es.B: Pero si {{plural_you:muestran|mostráis}} favoritismo, {{plural_you:cometen|cometéis}} pecado, y la ley {{plural_you:los|os}} declara culpables como infractores de la ley.
es.R: Pero si {{plural_you:favorecen|favorecéis}} a unas personas más que a otras, {{plural_you:están|estáis}} pecando. La ley demuestra que {{plural_you:son|sois}} culpables de quebrantarla.

fr.L: Mais si vous faites preuve de partialité, vous commettez un péché, étant convaincus par la Loi comme transgresseurs.
fr.B: Mais si vous faites du favoritisme, vous commettez un péché, et la Loi vous déclare coupables d’infraction.
fr.R: Mais si vous préférez certaines personnes à d’autres, vous péchez. La Loi montre que vous êtes coupables de lui désobéir.

sw.L: Lakini mkiwapendelea watu, mnatenda dhambi, mkitiwa hatiani na sheria kama wavunjaji [wa sheria].
sw.B: Lakini mkiwapendelea watu, mnatenda dhambi, na sheria inawatia hatiani kuwa wavunjaji wa sheria.
sw.R: Lakini mkiwapendelea watu fulani kuliko wengine, mnatenda dhambi. Sheria inaonyesha kwamba mna hatia ya kuivunja.

decisions.choice: show favoritism: treat people by their status
decisions.reason: προσωπολημπτεῖτε is the verb from the noun in 2:1: to "lift the face" of someone, favoring the rich over the poor.

decisions.choice: convicted: exposed and proven guilty
decisions.reason: ἐλεγχόμενοι means to expose a wrong and prove it. The law itself is the witness against them, because it commands love of neighbor and forbids partiality (Leviticus 19:15, 18).

decisions.choice: transgressors: those who step over a set line
decisions.reason: παραβάτης is someone who breaks a definite command. Favoritism is not a small lapse in manners; it breaks God's law, and verses 10-11 explain why that makes them lawbreakers.

source.text: ὅστις γὰρ ὅλον τὸν νόμον τηρήσῃ, πταίσῃ δὲ ἐν ἑνί, γέγονεν πάντων ἔνοχος.

records.literal_gloss: Whoever for whole the law keeps, stumbles but in one, has become of all guilty.

en.L: For whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles in one [point] has become guilty of all.
en.B: For if someone keeps the entire law and yet stumbles at one point, that person has become guilty of breaking all of it.
en.R: Suppose someone obeys the whole law except for one command. That person is guilty of breaking the whole law.

es.L: Porque cualquiera que guarde toda la ley, pero tropiece en un [punto], se ha hecho culpable de todos.
es.B: Porque si alguien guarda la ley entera, pero tropieza en un solo punto, se ha hecho culpable de quebrantarla toda.
es.R: Supongamos que alguien obedece toda la ley menos un mandamiento. Esa persona es culpable de quebrantar toda la ley.

fr.L: Car quiconque garde la Loi entière mais trébuche sur un seul [point] est devenu coupable de tous.
fr.B: Car si quelqu’un observe toute la Loi et trébuche pourtant sur un seul point, il est devenu coupable de l’avoir enfreinte tout entière.
fr.R: Imaginons que quelqu’un obéisse à toute la Loi, sauf à un seul commandement. Il est coupable d’avoir désobéi à toute la Loi.

sw.L: Kwa maana yeyote atakayeishika sheria yote, lakini akajikwaa katika [jambo] moja, amekuwa na hatia ya yote.
sw.B: Kwa maana mtu akiishika sheria yote, lakini akajikwaa katika jambo moja tu, amekuwa na hatia ya kuivunja yote.
sw.R: Tuseme mtu anaitii sheria yote isipokuwa amri moja. Mtu huyo ana hatia ya kuivunja sheria nzima.

decisions.choice: guilty of all: the law is one, because the one who gave it is one
alternatives: guilty of breaking every single command
decisions.reason: James does not mean that one sin is the same as committing every sin. The law is one whole, the expression of one Lawgiver's will (2:11; 4:12), so breaking any part of it makes a person a lawbreaker. ἔνοχος means liable, answerable before a court.

decisions.choice: a supposition: whoever should keep ... and stumble
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the subjunctive: James imagines a case to make his point. He does not suggest anyone keeps the whole law perfectly (3:2: all of us stumble in many things).

decisions.choice: guilty of breaking all of it; guilty of breaking the whole law
decisions.reason: "Guilty of all" is compressed in English. Balanced and Readable say what one is guilty of.

source.text: ὁ γὰρ εἰπών Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς εἶπεν καί Μὴ φονεύσῃς· εἰ δὲ οὐ μοιχεύεις φονεύεις δέ, γέγονας παραβάτης νόμου.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] for having said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not murder; if but not you commit adultery you murder but, you have become a transgressor of law.

en.L: For the one who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not murder." Now if you do not commit adultery but you murder, you have become a transgressor of [the] law.
en.B: For the one who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not murder." So if you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have still broken the law.
en.R: God gave the command "Do not commit adultery," and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also gave the command "Do not murder." So if you never commit adultery but you murder someone, you are still a lawbreaker.

es.L: Porque el que dijo: «No cometas adulterio», dijo también: «No asesines». Ahora bien, si no cometes adulterio, pero asesinas, te has hecho transgresor de [la] ley.
es.B: Porque el que dijo: «No cometas adulterio», también dijo: «No asesines». Así que, si no cometes adulterio pero sí asesinas, igual has quebrantado la ley.
es.R: Dios dio el mandamiento «No cometas adulterio», y también dio el mandamiento «No asesines». Así que, si nunca cometes adulterio, pero asesinas a alguien, de todos modos has quebrantado la ley.

fr.L: Car celui qui a dit : « Ne commets pas d’adultère », a dit aussi : « Ne tue pas. » Or si tu ne commets pas d’adultère mais que tu tues, tu es devenu transgresseur de la Loi.
fr.B: Car celui qui a dit : « Ne commets pas d’adultère », a dit aussi : « Ne tue pas. » Si donc tu ne commets pas d’adultère mais que tu tues, tu as quand même enfreint la Loi.
fr.R: Dieu a donné le commandement « Ne commets pas d’adultère », et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a aussi donné le commandement « Ne tue pas ». Alors, si tu ne commets jamais d’adultère mais que tu tues quelqu’un, tu désobéis quand même à la Loi.

sw.L: Kwa maana yeye aliyesema, "Usizini," alisema pia, "Usiue." Basi, ikiwa huzini lakini unaua, umekuwa mvunjaji wa sheria.
sw.B: Kwa maana yule aliyesema, "Usizini," ndiye aliyesema pia, "Usiue." Kwa hiyo, ikiwa huzini lakini unaua, bado umeivunja sheria.
sw.R: Mungu alitoa amri, "Usizini," na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} pia alitoa amri, "Usiue." Kwa hiyo, kama hujawahi kuzini lakini umeua mtu, wewe bado ni mvunjaji wa sheria.

decisions.choice: Do not commit adultery; Do not murder: the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: James quotes two of the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:13-14; Deuteronomy 5:17-18). He names adultery first, as Luke 18:20 and Romans 13:9 also do.

decisions.choice: the one who said: God, the one Lawgiver
decisions.reason: The commands have one source. Since the same God gave them all, obeying some and breaking others is still disobeying him (4:12 speaks of one lawgiver and judge).

decisions.choice: a transgressor of law: a lawbreaker, of the law as a whole
decisions.reason: νόμου has no article, which stresses what kind of person one becomes: a lawbreaker. The law in view is still the one law of verse 10.

decisions.choice: God gave the command
decisions.reason: Readable names God, the speaker the Greek refers to (see the meaning decision).

decisions.choice: y también dio el mandamiento
alternatives: y él también dio el mandamiento
decisions.reason: Spanish needs no subject pronoun here, so the English Readable's capitalisable "he" has no Spanish counterpart and there is no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: tu
decisions.reason: James turns here to a single imagined reader: the verbs are singular, which English "you" cannot show. French follows the Greek number, as in 2:18-22.

source.text: οὕτως λαλεῖτε καὶ οὕτως ποιεῖτε ὡς διὰ νόμου ἐλευθερίας μέλλοντες κρίνεσθαι.

records.literal_gloss: So speak and so do as by law of freedom being about to be judged.

en.L: So speak and so act as [those who are] about to be judged by [the] law of freedom.
en.B: Speak and act as people who are going to be judged by the law of freedom.
en.R: One day you will be judged by the law of freedom. So let that guide the way you speak and the way you act.

es.L: Así {{plural_you:hablen|hablad}} y así {{plural_you:actúen|actuad}}, como [quienes] van a ser juzgados por [la] ley de [la] libertad.
es.B: {{plural_you:Hablen|Hablad}} y {{plural_you:actúen|actuad}} como quienes van a ser juzgados por la ley de la libertad.
es.R: Un día {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} juzgados por la ley de la libertad. Por eso, {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} que eso guíe {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} manera de hablar y {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} manera de actuar.

fr.L: Parlez ainsi et agissez ainsi, comme [des gens qui] doivent être jugés par la loi de la liberté.
fr.B: Parlez et agissez comme des gens qui vont être jugés par la loi de la liberté.
fr.R: Un jour, vous serez jugés par la loi de la liberté. Alors, que cela guide votre manière de parler et votre manière d’agir.

sw.L: Semeni hivyo na tendeni hivyo kama [watu] walio karibu kuhukumiwa kwa sheria ya uhuru.
sw.B: Semeni na kutenda kama watu watakaohukumiwa kwa sheria ya uhuru.
sw.R: Siku moja mtahukumiwa kwa sheria ya uhuru. Kwa hiyo, acheni jambo hilo liongoze jinsi mnavyosema na jinsi mnavyotenda.

decisions.choice: the law of freedom: God's law as it is given in the kingdom, the law that sets people free
alternatives: a law that gives permission to do as one likes
decisions.reason: James has called it "the perfect law of freedom" (1:25) and "the royal law" (2:8). It is God's law summed up in love of neighbor, which frees those who keep it rather than enslaving them (Psalm 119:45; John 8:31-32).

decisions.choice: as people about to be judged: the coming judgment is certain
decisions.reason: μέλλοντες with an infinitive speaks of what is sure to happen. The standard of judgment is the same law: God will look at how they spoke and acted toward others, including the poor.

decisions.choice: speak and act: words and deeds together
decisions.reason: James joins speaking and doing, as he joins hearing and doing (1:22). Their words to the rich and poor man (2:3) and their words to the hungry (2:16) will be judged along with their deeds.

decisions.choice: judgment first, then the command
decisions.reason: Readable states the fact first and then what follows from it, in two short sentences.

source.text: ἡ γὰρ κρίσις ἀνέλεος τῷ μὴ ποιήσαντι ἔλεος· κατακαυχᾶται ἔλεος κρίσεως.

records.literal_gloss: The for judgment merciless to the [one] not having done mercy; boasts against mercy judgment.

en.L: For the judgment [will be] merciless to the one who has not shown mercy; mercy boasts against judgment.
en.B: Judgment will have no mercy on the one who has shown no mercy. Mercy wins out over judgment.
en.R: People who have not shown mercy will be judged without mercy. But mercy is stronger than judgment.

es.L: Porque el juicio [será] sin misericordia para el que no ha mostrado misericordia; la misericordia se jacta frente al juicio.
es.B: El juicio no tendrá misericordia de quien no ha tenido misericordia. La misericordia triunfa sobre el juicio.
es.R: Los que no han mostrado misericordia serán juzgados sin misericordia. Pero la misericordia es más fuerte que el juicio.

fr.L: Car le jugement [sera] sans miséricorde envers celui qui n’a pas usé de miséricorde ; la miséricorde se glorifie face au jugement.
fr.B: Le jugement sera sans pitié pour celui qui n’a pas eu pitié. La miséricorde l’emporte sur le jugement.
fr.R: Ceux qui n’ont pas eu pitié des autres seront jugés sans pitié. Mais la pitié est plus forte que le jugement.

sw.L: Kwa maana hukumu [itakuwa] bila rehema kwa yule asiyeonyesha rehema; rehema inajisifu mbele ya hukumu.
sw.B: Hukumu haitakuwa na rehema kwa mtu asiyeonyesha rehema. Rehema hushinda hukumu.
sw.R: Watu ambao hawajaonyesha rehema watahukumiwa bila rehema. Lakini rehema ina nguvu kuliko hukumu.

decisions.choice: judgment will be merciless: the future judgment of God
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb in the first clause. It continues verse 12, so the judgment is God's coming judgment. Jesus taught the same: "Blessed are the merciful, because mercy will be shown to them" (Matthew 5:7; 18:33-35).

decisions.choice: boasts against: triumphs over, stands unafraid before
decisions.reason: κατακαυχᾶται means to boast in triumph over someone. Mercy can face judgment without fear and win.

decisions.choice: mercy shown by people stands firm at the judgment
decisions.reason: The first clause speaks of those who show mercy or do not, so the mercy here is most likely the mercy a person has shown: it has nothing to fear at the judgment. Others take it as God's mercy, which is greater than his judgment. The two belong together, since those who show mercy are those who have received it (Matthew 18:33).

decisions.choice: wins out over; is stronger than
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the image of boasting. Balanced and Readable give its point, victory.

decisions.choice: sans miséricorde … miséricorde (L); sans pitié … pitié, then miséricorde (B); pitié throughout (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek repeats one word. Literal keeps "miséricorde" each time; Balanced says the first saying with the everyday "pitié", which keeps the repetition, and the closing proverb with "miséricorde"; Readable keeps the plain word throughout.

source.text: Τί ὄφελος, ἀδελφοί μου, ἐὰν πίστιν λέγῃ τις ἔχειν ἔργα δὲ μὴ ἔχῃ;

records.literal_gloss: What [is] the profit, brothers of me, if faith says someone to have works but not he has?

en.L: What [is the] profit, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, if anyone says [he] has faith but has no works?
en.B: What use is it, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, for someone to claim faith if that person has no works?
en.R: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, what good is it if people say they have faith, but they have no actions to go with it?

es.L: ¿Qué provecho [hay], hermanos míos, si alguien dice tener fe, pero no tiene obras?
es.B: ¿De qué sirve, hermanos míos, que alguien afirme tener fe, si no tiene obras?
es.R: Hermanos míos, ¿de qué sirve que alguien diga que tiene fe, si no tiene obras que lo demuestren?

fr.L: Quel profit [y a-t-il], mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, si quelqu’un dit avoir la foi mais n’a pas d’œuvres ?
fr.B: À quoi cela sert-il, mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, que quelqu’un prétende avoir la foi, s’il n’a pas d’œuvres ?
fr.R: Mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, à quoi bon dire qu’on a la foi, si on n’a pas d’actions qui vont avec ?

sw.L: Kuna faida gani, ndugu zangu, mtu akisema ana imani lakini hana matendo?
sw.B: Ndugu zangu, inafaa nini mtu kudai kuwa na imani ikiwa hana matendo?
sw.R: Ndugu zangu, ni faida gani watu wakisema wana imani, lakini hawana matendo yanayoendana nayo?

decisions.choice: says he has faith: a claim to faith
decisions.reason: James does not say "if someone has faith" but "if someone says he has faith". The whole argument of 2:14-26 is about a faith that is only claimed, and verse 18 asks for it to be shown.

decisions.choice: works: the deeds that faith does, above all deeds of love and mercy
alternatives: works of the law, keeping the commands that set Jews apart, such as circumcision
decisions.reason: ἔργον here means what a person does. The examples are feeding and clothing a brother or sister (2:15-16), Abraham's offering of Isaac (2:21) and Rahab's sheltering of the messengers (2:25). They are not the "works of the law" that Paul says do not justify (Romans 3:28; Galatians 2:16).

decisions.choice: what profit: what good does it do
decisions.reason: ὄφελος is benefit, advantage. James asks what such faith does for the one who has it, and the next sentence answers: it cannot save. He asks the same question of empty words in 2:16.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: James is writing to the whole community of believers, women and men alike, so the inclusive form is the default; the traditional wording is the alternative.

decisions.choice: actions
decisions.reason: Readable says "actions" for ἔργον, a common word for what people do; Literal and Balanced keep "works" through 2:14-26 so that the argument's key word stays visible.

decisions.choice: obras at every level
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "actions" so that "works" is not heard as church jargon. Spanish "obras" is an everyday word for deeds, and keeping it at every level lets the reader follow James's one word through 2:14-26 and compare it with Paul's "obras de la ley".

decisions.choice: les œuvres (L, B); les actions (R) through 2:14-26
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal and Balanced keep the key word of the argument, so that it can be compared with Romans; Readable says "actions", the common word for what people do.

decisions.choice: matendo at every level
decisions.reason: "Matendo" (deeds) is the settled word for works and is everyday Swahili, so it serves Readable too, where the English says "actions". It is the same word Romans uses for "matendo ya sheria", so James and Paul can be compared.

source.text: μὴ δύναται ἡ πίστις σῶσαι αὐτόν;

records.literal_gloss: Not is able the faith to save him?

en.L: That faith is not able to save {{gender:them|him}}, [is it]?
en.B: That faith cannot save the person, can it?
en.R: That kind of faith cannot save anyone, can it?

es.L: Esa fe no puede salvar a {{gender:esa persona|ese hombre}}, ¿[verdad]?
es.B: Una fe así no puede salvar a esa persona, ¿verdad?
es.R: Esa clase de fe no puede salvar a nadie, ¿verdad?

fr.L: La foi ne peut pas le sauver, [n’est-ce pas] ?
fr.B: Cette foi-là ne peut pas le sauver, n’est-ce pas ?
fr.R: Une foi comme celle-là ne peut sauver personne, n’est-ce pas ?

sw.L: Imani [hiyo] haiwezi kumwokoa, [sivyo]?
sw.B: Imani hiyo haiwezi kumwokoa mtu huyo, sivyo?
sw.R: Imani ya namna hiyo haiwezi kumwokoa mtu yeyote, sivyo?

decisions.choice: the faith: that faith, the faith just described
decisions.reason: The article points back to the faith someone claims but does not show in works. James does not say faith cannot save; he says this kind cannot.

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: μὴ at the start of a question expects "no": such faith cannot save.

decisions.choice: save: rescue at God's final judgment
decisions.reason: James has just spoken of judgment (2:12-13) and uses the same verb of the word that is able to save souls (1:21; also 4:12; 5:20). The question is whether such faith will stand when God judges.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to "anyone" (2:14), man or woman. Literal keeps a pronoun, inclusive by default; Balanced and Readable say "the person" and "anyone", which need no setting.

decisions.choice: le (L, B), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers back to "quelqu'un" and is ordinary generic French, so the English {{gender:them|him}} needs no span.

source.text: ἐὰν ἀδελφὸς ἢ ἀδελφὴ γυμνοὶ ὑπάρχωσιν καὶ λειπόμενοι τῆς ἐφημέρου τροφῆς, εἴπῃ δέ τις αὐτοῖς ἐξ ὑμῶν· Ὑπάγετε ἐν εἰρήνῃ, θερμαίνεσθε καὶ χορτάζεσθε, μὴ δῶτε δὲ αὐτοῖς τὰ ἐπιτήδεια τοῦ σώματος, τί ὄφελος;

records.literal_gloss: If a brother or a sister naked are and lacking the daily food, \v 16 says and someone to them from you, Go in peace, be warmed and be filled, not you give but to them the necessities of the body, what [is] the profit?

en.L: If a brother or a sister is naked and lacking the food for the day, \v 16 and one of you says to them, "Go in peace, be warmed and be filled," but you do not give them the necessities of the body, what [is the] profit?
en.B: Suppose a brother or sister has no proper clothes and not enough food for the day, \v 16 and one of you tells them, "Go in peace; keep warm and eat well," but you do not give them what the body needs. What use is that?
en.R: Imagine a brother or sister who has nothing to wear and nothing to eat today. \v 16 One of you says to them, "Go in peace! Keep warm and eat all you want!" But none of you gives them anything their body needs. What good is that?

es.L: Si un hermano o una hermana están desnudos y les falta el alimento del día, \v 16 y alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} les dice: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} en paz, {{plural_you:caliéntense|calentaos}} y {{plural_you:sáciense|saciaos}}», pero no les {{plural_you:dan|dais}} lo necesario para el cuerpo, ¿qué provecho [hay]?
es.B: Supongamos que un hermano o una hermana no tienen ropa suficiente ni comida para el día, \v 16 y uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} les dice: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} en paz; {{plural_you:abríguense|abrigaos}} y {{plural_you:coman|comed}} bien», pero no les {{plural_you:dan|dais}} lo que el cuerpo necesita. ¿De qué sirve eso?
es.R: {{plural_you:Imaginen|Imaginad}} a un hermano o una hermana que no tiene nada que ponerse ni nada que comer hoy. \v 16 Uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} les dice: «¡{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} en paz! ¡{{plural_you:Abríguense|Abrigaos}} y {{plural_you:coman todo lo que quieran|comed todo lo que queráis}}!». Pero ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} les da nada de lo que su cuerpo necesita. ¿De qué sirve eso?

fr.L: Si un frère ou une sœur sont nus et manquent de la nourriture du jour, \v 16 et que l’un de vous leur dise : « Allez en paix, soyez réchauffés et rassasiés », mais que vous ne leur donniez pas ce qui est nécessaire au corps, quel profit [y a-t-il] ?
fr.B: Supposons qu’un frère ou une sœur n’aient pas de quoi se vêtir et n’aient pas assez à manger pour la journée, \v 16 et que l’un de vous leur dise : « Allez en paix ; couvrez-vous bien et mangez à votre faim », sans que vous leur donniez ce dont le corps a besoin. À quoi cela sert-il ?
fr.R: Imaginez un frère ou une sœur qui n’a rien à se mettre et rien à manger aujourd’hui. \v 16 L’un de vous leur dit : « Allez en paix ! Restez au chaud et mangez autant que vous voulez ! » Mais personne parmi vous ne leur donne ce dont leur corps a besoin. À quoi cela sert-il ?

sw.L: Ikiwa ndugu wa kiume au wa kike wako uchi na wanakosa chakula cha siku hiyo, \v 16 na mmoja wenu akawaambia, "Nendeni kwa amani, mpate joto na mshibe," lakini hamwapi mahitaji ya mwili, kuna faida gani?
sw.B: Tuseme ndugu wa kiume au wa kike hana nguo za kutosha wala chakula cha siku hiyo, \v 16 na mmoja wenu akawaambia, "Nendeni kwa amani; mpate joto na mle mshibe," lakini hamwapi mahitaji ya mwili. Inafaa nini?
sw.R: Fikirini ndugu wa kiume au wa kike asiye na nguo za kuvaa wala chakula cha kula leo. \v 16 Mmoja wenu anawaambia, "Nendeni kwa amani! Mjipashe moto na mle mpaka mshibe!" Lakini hakuna hata mmoja wenu anayewapa chochote ambacho miili yao inahitaji. Kuna faida gani?

decisions.choice: naked: without proper clothing
decisions.reason: γυμνοὶ can mean wearing only an undergarment, without the outer cloak that kept a person warm at night (Exodus 22:26-27; John 21:7). Hence "keep warm" in verse 16.

decisions.choice: the food for the day: what is needed to eat today
decisions.reason: ἐφημέρου means "for the day". They do not have even today's food, which is what Jesus taught his followers to pray for (Matthew 6:11).

decisions.choice: Go in peace: a customary farewell
decisions.reason: "Go in peace" was an everyday blessing at parting (Judges 18:6; 1 Samuel 1:17; Mark 5:34). Here it is a kind word used to send needy people away empty-handed.

decisions.choice: one of you says, but you do not give: the whole church shares the blame
decisions.reason: "One of you" speaks, but the verb "give" is plural: none of them helps. The community that lets the words stand without the help is responsible together.

decisions.choice: a brother or sister
decisions.reason: The Greek names both, so English does too; no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: keep warm and eat well; Keep warm and eat all you want
decisions.reason: The verbs can be middle ("warm yourselves") or passive ("be warmed"); either way they are wishes with no help behind them. Balanced and Readable give them as the casual well-wishing they are.

decisions.choice: plural_you on the farewell to the brother and sister
decisions.reason: The farewell is spoken to two people, not to James's readers, but a reader who has chosen vosotros would find "Vayan en paz" foreign, so the commands follow the same setting ("Vayan" | "Id").

decisions.choice: ndugu wa kiume au wa kike
decisions.reason: Swahili "ndugu" covers both ἀδελφὸς and ἀδελφὴ, so "wa kiume" and "wa kike" are added to keep James's two words apart. "Dada" would also work but is more often a sister by birth.

source.text: οὕτως καὶ ἡ πίστις, ἐὰν μὴ ἔχῃ ἔργα, νεκρά ἐστιν καθ’ ἑαυτήν.

records.literal_gloss: So also the faith, if not it has works, dead is by itself.

en.L: So also faith, if it does not have works, is dead in itself.
en.B: It is the same with faith: if it has no works, it is dead in itself.
en.R: Faith is like that too. If faith has no actions, it is completely dead.

es.L: Así también la fe, si no tiene obras, está muerta en sí misma.
es.B: Lo mismo pasa con la fe: si no tiene obras, está muerta en sí misma.
es.R: Con la fe pasa lo mismo. Si la fe no tiene obras, está completamente muerta.

fr.L: De même aussi la foi, si elle n’a pas d’œuvres, est morte par elle-même.
fr.B: C’est pareil pour la foi : si elle reste sans œuvres, elle est morte en elle-même.
fr.R: La foi, c’est pareil. Si la foi n’a pas d’actions, elle est complètement morte.

sw.L: Hivyo pia imani, ikiwa haina matendo, imekufa ndani yake yenyewe.
sw.B: Ndivyo ilivyo kwa imani: ikiwa haina matendo, imekufa ndani yake yenyewe.
sw.R: Imani nayo ni hivyo hivyo. Imani isiyo na matendo imekufa kabisa.

decisions.choice: dead: without life, unable to do what living faith does
decisions.reason: νεκρά does not mean weak but lifeless. James repeats it in 2:26: like a body without the spirit.

decisions.choice: in itself: dead through and through
alternatives: by itself, when it stands alone
decisions.reason: καθ ἑαυτήν can mean "in itself", that is, inwardly dead and not merely looking dead from outside, or "by itself", alone without works. The first is the more natural sense of the phrase; the second says what verses 18-26 also say.

decisions.choice: completely dead
decisions.reason: Readable gives the force of "in itself" in plain words.

source.text: Ἀλλ’ ἐρεῖ τις· Σὺ πίστιν ἔχεις κἀγὼ ἔργα ἔχω.

records.literal_gloss: But will say someone, You faith have and I works have.

en.L: But someone will say, "You have faith, and I have works."
en.B: But someone will say, "You have faith, and I have works."
en.R: But someone will say, "One person has faith, and another has actions."

es.L: Pero alguien dirá: «Tú tienes fe, y yo tengo obras».
es.B: Pero alguien dirá: «Tú tienes fe, y yo tengo obras».
es.R: Pero alguien dirá: «Una persona tiene fe, y otra tiene obras».

fr.L: Mais quelqu’un dira : « Toi, tu as la foi, et moi, j’ai des œuvres. »
fr.B: Mais quelqu’un dira : « Toi, tu as la foi ; moi, j’ai les œuvres. »
fr.R: Mais quelqu’un dira : « Une personne a la foi, et une autre a des actions. »

sw.L: Lakini mtu atasema, "Wewe una imani, nami nina matendo."
sw.B: Lakini mtu atasema, "Wewe una imani, nami nina matendo."
sw.R: Lakini mtu atasema, "Mtu mmoja ana imani, na mwingine ana matendo."

decisions.choice: the speaker's words are only "You have faith, and I have works", as the SBLGNT punctuates
alternatives: the quotation runs on to the end of verse 18 or 19
the speaker is on James's side
decisions.reason: The Greek has no quotation marks, and where this speaker stops is one of the hardest questions in the letter. The SBLGNT ends the quotation after "I have works", so the next sentence is James's reply. This record follows it.

decisions.choice: "you" and "I" mean "one person" and "another": faith and works are separate gifts
alternatives: the speaker is an ally who has works, speaking to the one who has only faith
decisions.reason: Read with the SBLGNT's punctuation, the objector seems to say that faith and works can be found in different people, so that one may have the first without the second. James answers that faith cannot be shown without works. Others hear an ally supporting James, but "But someone will say" usually introduces an objection (1 Corinthians 15:35; Romans 9:19).

decisions.choice: One person has faith, and another has actions
alternatives: You have faith, and I have works
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the meaning chosen in the meaning decision: "you" and "I" stand for any two people.

decisions.choice: actions
decisions.reason: Readable says "actions" for ἔργον, a common word for what people do; Literal and Balanced keep "works" through 2:14-26 so that the argument's key word stays visible.

source.text: δεῖξόν μοι τὴν πίστιν σου χωρὶς τῶν ἔργων, κἀγώ σοι δείξω ἐκ τῶν ἔργων μου τὴν πίστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Show me the faith of you without the works, and I to you will show by the works of me the faith.

en.L: Show me your faith without the works, and I will show you, by my works, [my] faith.
en.B: Show me your faith without any works, and I will show you my faith by means of my works.
en.R: Show me your faith if you have no actions! I will show you my faith by what I do.

es.L: Muéstrame tu fe sin las obras, y yo te mostraré por mis obras [mi] fe.
es.B: Muéstrame tu fe sin obras, y yo te mostraré mi fe por medio de mis obras.
es.R: ¡Muéstrame tu fe si no tienes obras! Yo te mostraré mi fe por lo que hago.

fr.L: Montre-moi ta foi sans les œuvres, et moi, à partir de mes œuvres, je te montrerai [ma] foi.
fr.B: Montre-moi ta foi sans aucune œuvre, et moi, c’est par mes œuvres que je te montrerai ma foi.
fr.R: Montre-moi ta foi, si tu n’as pas d’actions ! Moi, je te montrerai ma foi par ce que je fais.

sw.L: Nionyeshe imani yako bila matendo, nami nitakuonyesha kwa matendo yangu imani [yangu].
sw.B: Nionyeshe imani yako isiyo na matendo yoyote, nami nitakudhihirishia imani yangu kupitia matendo yangu.
sw.R: Nionyeshe imani yako kama huna matendo! Mimi nitakuonyesha imani yangu kwa yale ninayotenda.

decisions.choice: show me your faith without works: a challenge that cannot be met
decisions.reason: δεῖξόν is an imperative, but James means it as a challenge: faith cannot be seen apart from what it does. The point is not that works replace faith but that works are how faith is seen.

decisions.choice: by my works ... my faith: faith made visible through what it does
decisions.reason: James does not set his works against his faith. He will show the faith itself, by means of the works that come from it, as Abraham's faith was seen in what he did (2:22).

decisions.choice: by what I do
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the plain verb here; "actions" stands earlier in the sentence.

source.text: σὺ πιστεύεις ὅτι εἷς ἐστιν ὁ θεός;

records.literal_gloss: You believe that one is the God?

en.L: You believe that God is one?
en.B: You believe that God is one?
en.R: Do you believe that God is one, that there is only one God?

es.L: ¿Tú crees que Dios es uno?
es.B: ¿Tú crees que Dios es uno?
es.R: ¿Crees que Dios es uno, que solo hay un Dios?

fr.L: Toi, tu crois que Dieu est un ?
fr.B: Tu crois que Dieu est un ?
fr.R: Crois-tu que Dieu est un, qu’il n’y a qu’un seul Dieu ?

sw.L: Wewe unaamini kwamba Mungu ni mmoja?
sw.B: Je, unaamini kwamba Mungu ni mmoja?
sw.R: Je, unaamini kwamba Mungu ni mmoja, kwamba kuna Mungu mmoja tu?

decisions.choice: God is one: the Shema, Deuteronomy 6:4
decisions.reason: "Hear, Israel: the LORD is our God; the LORD is one" (Deuteronomy 6:4). It was the central confession of Israel's faith, recited daily, and Jesus called it the first command (Mark 12:29). James's readers would all have confessed it.

decisions.choice: a question, as the SBLGNT punctuates
alternatives: a statement: "You believe that God is one."
decisions.reason: The Greek words can be read as a statement or as a question; the SBLGNT has a question mark. The meaning is the same: the reader holds the right belief.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "God is one"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ in the order of these words and in whether "God" has the article, and some can be read as "there is one God". The confession is the same in all of them. From general knowledge; reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: that there is only one God
decisions.reason: Readable adds what the confession means, so a new reader does not take "one" as a number to count.

source.text: καλῶς ποιεῖς· καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια πιστεύουσιν καὶ φρίσσουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Well you do; also the demons believe and shudder.

en.L: You do well; the demons also believe, and they shudder.
en.B: Well and good! The demons believe it too, and they tremble.
en.R: That is good! But the demons believe that as well, and they shake with fear.

es.L: Haces bien; también los demonios creen, y se estremecen.
es.B: ¡Muy bien! También los demonios lo creen, y tiemblan.
es.R: ¡Eso está bien! Pero los demonios también lo creen, y tiemblan de miedo.

fr.L: Tu fais bien ; les démons aussi croient, et ils frissonnent.
fr.B: Très bien ! Les démons aussi le croient, et ils tremblent.
fr.R: C’est bien ! Mais les démons aussi le croient, et ils tremblent de peur.

sw.L: Unafanya vizuri; pepo nao wanaamini, na wanatetemeka.
sw.B: Vema sana! Pepo pia wanaamini hivyo, nao wanatetemeka.
sw.R: Hilo ni jema! Lakini hata pepo wanaamini hivyo, nao wanatetemeka kwa hofu.

decisions.choice: you do well: real approval, with an edge
decisions.reason: καλῶς ποιεῖς approves of the belief: it is true. But in the next breath James shows that agreeing with a true statement is not the faith he means. It is the same phrase as in 2:8.

decisions.choice: believe: hold to be true, without trust or obedience
decisions.reason: The demons believe the same thing: they know who God is (Mark 1:24; 5:7). Belief that only agrees with the facts is not the faith that saves.

decisions.choice: shudder: tremble with terror
decisions.reason: φρίσσουσιν means to bristle or shudder with fear. The demons' belief brings no peace, only dread of the God they know will judge them.

source.text: θέλεις δὲ γνῶναι, ὦ ἄνθρωπε κενέ, ὅτι ἡ πίστις χωρὶς τῶν ἔργων ἀργή ἐστιν;

records.literal_gloss: Want you and to know, O man empty, that the faith without the works useless is?

en.L: And do you want to know, O empty {{gender:person|man}}, that faith without the works is useless?
en.B: Do you want to be shown, you empty-headed {{gender:person|man}}, that faith without works does no work?
en.R: You foolish {{gender:person|man}}! Do you want me to show you that faith without actions is good for nothing?

es.L: ¿Y quieres saber, oh {{gender:persona vacía|hombre vacío}}, que la fe sin las obras es inútil?
es.B: ¿Quieres que te demuestre, {{gender:persona insensata|hombre insensato}}, que la fe sin obras no obra?
es.R: ¡{{gender:Persona necia|Hombre necio}}! ¿Quieres que te muestre que la fe sin obras no sirve para nada?

fr.L: Mais veux-tu savoir, ô {{gender:être humain|homme}} creux, que la foi sans les œuvres est inactive ?
fr.B: Veux-tu qu’on te le montre, esprit creux : la foi sans les œuvres est désœuvrée ?
fr.R: Que tu es bête ! Veux-tu que je te montre que la foi sans actions ne sert à rien ?

sw.L: Na unataka kujua, ewe mtu mtupu, kwamba imani bila matendo ni ya bure?
sw.B: Je, unataka kuonyeshwa, ewe mtu usiye na akili, kwamba imani isiyo na matendo haitendi chochote?
sw.R: Ewe mtu mpumbavu! Unataka nikuonyeshe kwamba imani isiyo na matendo haifai kitu?

decisions.choice: empty person: senseless, without substance
decisions.reason: κενέ means empty. The one who holds an empty faith is himself empty-headed. James addresses the objector of verse 18 directly, as Paul does in Romans 2:1 and 9:20.

decisions.choice: useless: idle, not working
decisions.reason: ἀργή means idle, unproductive. It is a play on words: the adjective is formed from the word for "work", so faith without works is a faith that does not work.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "useless"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts, including the later majority, read νεκρά ("dead") here, the word of verses 17 and 26; copyists may have brought this verse into line with those. The SBLGNT reads ἀργή, which has strong early support and is the harder reading. From general knowledge; reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:person|man}}
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωπε addresses an imagined objector who could be anyone, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: does no work
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the wordplay between works and a faith that does not work.

decisions.choice: {{gender:persona vacía|hombre vacío}}
decisions.reason: Spanish has two ways to address ἄνθρωπε, "persona" and "hombre", so the gender setting carries over from the English; the adjective agrees with each option.

decisions.choice: ô {{gender:être humain|homme}} creux (L); esprit creux (B) and "Que tu es bête !" (R), with no span
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the noun with the setting. Balanced and Readable address the objector with words that fit a man or a woman alike ("esprit creux", "bête"), so they need no setting where the English has one.

decisions.choice: désœuvrée (B); inactive (L)
decisions.reason: The word means idle, not working (m2), and plays on "works". French "désœuvrée", idle, is built on "œuvre" and keeps the wordplay the English Balanced keeps with "does no work".

decisions.choice: haitendi chochote
decisions.reason: ἀργή (idle, not working) plays on ἔργων. "Matendo" and "haitendi" share the root -tenda, so Swahili keeps the wordplay, as the English Balanced does with "works ... no work".

source.text: Ἀβραὰμ ὁ πατὴρ ἡμῶν οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη, ἀνενέγκας Ἰσαὰκ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον;

records.literal_gloss: Abraham the father of us not by works was justified, having offered up Isaac the son of him upon the altar?

en.L: Abraham our father, was he not justified by works, having offered up Isaac his son upon the altar?
en.B: Take Abraham our father: was it not by works that he was justified, when he offered up his son Isaac on the altar?
en.R: Think about our father Abraham. Was he not counted righteous because of his actions, when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?

es.L: Abraham nuestro padre, ¿no fue justificado por obras, cuando ofreció a Isaac su hijo sobre el altar?
es.B: Pensemos en Abraham, nuestro padre: ¿no fue por las obras que fue justificado, cuando ofreció a su hijo Isaac sobre el altar?
es.R: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} en nuestro padre Abraham. ¿No fue declarado justo por sus obras, cuando ofreció a su hijo Isaac sobre el altar?

fr.L: Abraham notre père n’a-t-il pas été justifié par les œuvres, ayant offert Isaac son fils sur l’autel ?
fr.B: Prenez Abraham notre père : n’est-ce pas par les œuvres qu’il a été déclaré juste, quand il a offert son fils Isaac sur l’autel ?
fr.R: Pensez à notre père Abraham. Dieu ne l’a-t-il pas reconnu juste à cause de ses actions, quand il a offert son fils Isaac sur l’autel ?

sw.L: Ibrahimu baba yetu, je, hakuhesabiwa haki kutokana na matendo, alipomtoa Isaka mwanawe kuwa sadaka juu ya madhabahu?
sw.B: Mfikirie Ibrahimu baba yetu: je, si kwa matendo alihesabiwa haki, alipomtoa mwanawe Isaka sadaka juu ya madhabahu?
sw.R: Fikirini habari ya baba yetu Ibrahimu. Je, hakuhesabiwa haki kwa sababu ya matendo yake, alipomtoa mwanawe Isaka kuwa sadaka madhabahuni?

decisions.choice: justified: declared to be in the right by God
alternatives: shown to be righteous, proved right before others
decisions.reason: δικαιόω means to declare or acknowledge someone as being in the right, as a judge does. The setting is God's judgment (2:12-13), so the verdict is God's. Some take it here to mean "shown to be righteous", proved by what he did. The two readings are close: in both, Abraham's faith is seen to be real in the offering of Isaac.

decisions.choice: the offering of Isaac: Genesis 22
decisions.reason: In Genesis 22:1-19 God tested Abraham by asking him to offer Isaac. Abraham bound him on the altar, and God stopped him and said, "now I know that you fear God" (22:12). The participle ἀνενέγκας says what he did: he brought his son to the altar and was ready to give him up (Hebrews 11:17).

decisions.choice: our father: Abraham as the ancestor of God's people
decisions.reason: Jewish readers called Abraham "our father" (John 8:39, 53). Paul also calls him the father of all who believe (Romans 4:11-12, 16).

decisions.choice: counted righteous
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "justified", the word the argument turns on, so that James 2:21-25 can be compared with Romans 3-4. Readable says "counted righteous", which says in plain words what the verdict is (see the meaning decision on δικαιόω).

decisions.choice: his actions
decisions.reason: Readable says "actions" for ἔργον, a common word for what people do; Literal and Balanced keep "works" through 2:14-26 so that the argument's key word stays visible.

decisions.choice: fue justificado (L, B); fue declarado justo (R)
decisions.reason: James uses the same verb as Paul, and the translation uses the same Spanish words as Romans and Galatians, "justificar" (Literal, Balanced) and "declarar justo" (Readable), so a reader can see that the two writers share one verb and weigh them side by side (see the meaning decision at 2:24). Readable says "declarado justo" where the English Readable says "counted righteous", to match Spanish Romans.

decisions.choice: justifier (L); déclarer juste (B); reconnaître juste (R) (for the whole book: 2:21, 2:24, 2:25)
alternatives: mettre en règle avec Dieu (R), as in Romans
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced follow the term sheet, so that James 2:21-25 can be compared with Romans 3-4. The English Readable says "counted righteous" here, the verdict God gives, so French Readable says "Dieu l'a reconnu juste" rather than Romans' "mis en règle avec Dieu".

decisions.choice: kuhesabiwa haki
decisions.reason: James uses the same verb as Paul, and "kuhesabiwa haki" is the Swahili of Romans and Galatians at every level, so a reader can see that the two writers share one verb and weigh them side by side (see the meaning decision at 2:24).

source.text: βλέπεις ὅτι ἡ πίστις συνήργει τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἔργων ἡ πίστις ἐτελειώθη, καὶ ἐπληρώθη ἡ γραφὴ ἡ λέγουσα· Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην, καὶ φίλος θεοῦ ἐκλήθη.

records.literal_gloss: You see that the faith worked with the works of him, and by the works the faith was perfected, \v 23 and was fulfilled the Scripture the [one] saying, Believed and Abraham the God, and it was credited to him for righteousness, and friend of God he was called.

en.L: You see that faith was working along with his works, and from the works faith was brought to completion, \v 23 and the Scripture was fulfilled that says, "And Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him for righteousness," and he was called friend of God.
en.B: You can see that his faith worked together with his works, and his faith reached its goal through those works. \v 23 So the Scripture came true that says, "Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness," and he was called God's friend.
en.R: You can see that his faith and his actions were working together. His faith was made complete by what he did. \v 23 In this way the words of Scripture came true: "Abraham believed God, and God counted that as righteousness for him." And Abraham was called God's friend.

es.L: Ves que la fe actuaba junto con sus obras, y por las obras la fe fue llevada a su plenitud, \v 23 y se cumplió la Escritura que dice: «Y creyó Abraham a Dios, y le fue acreditado como justicia», y fue llamado amigo de Dios.
es.B: Puedes ver que su fe actuaba junto con sus obras, y que por medio de esas obras su fe alcanzó su meta. \v 23 Así se cumplió la Escritura que dice: «Abraham creyó a Dios, y eso se le acreditó como justicia», y fue llamado amigo de Dios.
es.R: Puedes ver que su fe y sus obras actuaban juntas. Su fe se completó por lo que hizo. \v 23 Así se cumplieron las palabras de la Escritura: «Abraham creyó a Dios, y Dios le acreditó esa fe como justicia». Y a Abraham lo llamaron amigo de Dios.

fr.L: Tu vois que la foi agissait avec ses œuvres, et que par les œuvres la foi a été rendue parfaite, \v 23 et l’Écriture a été accomplie, qui dit : « Or Abraham a cru Dieu, et cela lui a été compté comme justice », et il a été appelé ami de Dieu.
fr.B: Tu vois que sa foi agissait avec ses œuvres, et que par ces œuvres sa foi a atteint son but. \v 23 Ainsi s’est réalisée l’Écriture qui dit : « Abraham a cru Dieu, et cela lui a été compté comme justice », et il a été appelé ami de Dieu.
fr.R: Tu vois que sa foi et ses actions agissaient ensemble. Sa foi a été rendue complète par ce qu’il a fait. \v 23 Ainsi, les paroles de l’Écriture se sont réalisées : « Abraham a cru Dieu, et Dieu a compté cela comme justice. » Et Abraham a été appelé l’ami de Dieu.

sw.L: Unaona kwamba imani ilikuwa ikitenda kazi pamoja na matendo yake, na kwa matendo imani ilikamilishwa, \v 23 na Maandiko yakatimizwa yasemayo, "Naye Ibrahimu alimwamini Mungu, na [hilo] likahesabiwa kwake kuwa haki," naye akaitwa rafiki wa Mungu.
sw.B: Unaweza kuona kwamba imani yake ilifanya kazi pamoja na matendo yake, na kupitia matendo hayo imani yake ikafikia ukamilifu wake. \v 23 Hivyo yakatimia Maandiko yanayosema, "Ibrahimu alimwamini Mungu, na hilo likahesabiwa kwake kuwa haki," naye akaitwa rafiki wa Mungu.
sw.R: Unaweza kuona kwamba imani yake na matendo yake vilikuwa vikifanya kazi pamoja. Imani yake ilikamilishwa kwa yale aliyotenda. \v 23 Kwa njia hii maneno ya Maandiko yalitimia: "Ibrahimu alimwamini Mungu, na Mungu akamhesabu kuwa mwenye haki kwa sababu hiyo." Na Ibrahimu akaitwa rafiki wa Mungu.

decisions.choice: faith was working with his works: faith and works acting together
decisions.reason: συνήργει ("was working with") is in the imperfect: through Abraham's life his faith was at work in what he did. Faith was not idle (2:20) but active in his works.

decisions.choice: made complete: brought to its full goal
alternatives: made perfect, as if faith had been faulty before
decisions.reason: τελειόω means to bring something to its goal or full growth. Abraham's faith was real before Genesis 22, but in the offering of Isaac it reached the maturity James speaks of in 1:4.

decisions.choice: the Scripture fulfilled: Genesis 15:6 shown true in Genesis 22
